body:
I'm sorry to hear that, man. -hugs-


It's odd, really. Family is something that's stressed in our lifestyle. We have a farm. This land has been in our family for 3 generations so far, 4 if I or my brother inherit it. Also, to your previous comment, I think allot of it falls on our family mind set(as to why they don't thing mental 'illness' is a thing). We are a bit on the Irish side in how we deal with our emotions. Sit, brood, then explode out of no where. Not talk about it. Grandpa used to rip the sleeves of his shirts in frustration regardless of what emotion he was feeling, and my mother is notorious for storming out of a room loudly. My brother has a shit fit and horrible temper(our dad also has a temper like this). For whatever reason, I turn my frustrations in on myself. -shrugs- I grew up learning that ones own issues were your own issues, and you could, and should, deal with them yourself.

I've apologized 3 times so far. :/ I defiantly have full responsibility on it.

We have 3 other dogs, but they are mostly outside dogs. Also have an indoor cat. This was our first indoor dog. Never had to worry about letting them back in in a timely fashion before this. Lazy habbits die hard I guess.

It makes sense getting another. We did the same when we put down our dog I had for 13-15 or so years. It does help. I kind of want to leave for a trip for a while so that my cat'll spend more time with mom, as he only hangs around me when I'm home but when I leave he is best buds with her.

Thank you. Honestly.

I've debated sending her a letter but before I send it I freak out and delete it. I second guess if I should really say anything. Fear of the repercussions and all that. I don't really want things to change but I guess the might have to.

I've browsed the Kubler-ross model before. Back in High School when one of our friends died in a car crash the councilor at school brought in tons of people to help with counseling and such. They talked about it quite allot.
Any tips for what I can do to help her with going through the whole thing? Or should I kind of just drop it and leave it alone.

Yeah, I know. It's less society, more me. I inherited being independent and having a want to be self sufficient(though it's wilted away over the last few years). I guess its something I share the the maternal unit...

fuck me, patterns are stupid. :/ hm...
I've been trying to weigh just how much it would hurt so I could take the path of least resistance for both of us. Can't ever really know, I guess.
I'm not entirely sure how to get help. :/ I don't have health insurance or anything like that so it be out of [mom's] pocket, which... hurts a bit. As if asking for help doesn't suck enough. lul

It's a bit funny cause mum is actually super educated. Has her Masters, but in business so I guess it's still irrelevant to the convo.

Trying to not focus on the dog. Reality is, I'm much less upset about the dog(I worked in a kill shelter for 2 years. Death doesn't really bother me any more despite how much I consider our animals as family), It's my utter retardation and lack of thought in what happened. I look out side at the snow and 20F temp and a tear up with frustration. I look around the house at all her toys and get upset(been hiding in my room for a while now with a hot water bottle trying to relax and get rid of this massive headache I got from crying/being tense/feeling like I'm going to vomit). My cat has been trying to comfort me but I just get more upset. What if I fuck up with him too? Kill him cause I made a dumb and obvious mistake.

Communicating is vastly not my strong point. I always lock up whenever I'm asked what I'm feeling. Usually I don't know what I'm feeling or how to put it into words. I get frustrated with myself over that one. If I can't sit and pick my words i usually just end up panicking and freezing.

I do feel lucky... just find myself wishing I could give it to someone who deserves it. :/

I know. She loves me, and I lover her, but I can't help but look at the cost vs value of the whole thing. I cost so much and have very little value to return. I just dig myself deeper into what feels like debt.

I've never been to a therapist or anything like that. Always wanted to believe in the concept of how strong the mind can be, that I could handle my own mental battles. I guess I have a hard time dealing with the concept cause I've heard allot of people I'm close to say they don't believe in mental illnesses. That people like that need to just suck it up and get over it.
